reviews.body:
## Pull request overview Implements Issue #30’s “immutable patch epoch” building blocks in `uor-r4-core` by introducing a `GraphPatch` delta format (added edges / residual updates / tombstones), a route-translation map, CBOR serialization, BLAKE3-based content IDs, and a basic Theorem 11 consistency verifier, with accompanying tests. **Changes:** - Add new `transformerless::graph_patch` module with `GraphPatch`, route translation mapping, CID hashing, CBOR encode/decode, in-place patch application, and a Theorem 11 verifier. - Derive `serde::{Serialize, Deserialize}` for `EdgeKind`, `Edge`, and `ScoreQ` to support patch serialization. - Add unit tests covering patch application, route translation mapping behavior, and CBOR round-tripping. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/graph_patch_test.rs | Adds tests for patch application, route translation mapping, and CBOR roundtrip. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/transitions.rs | Adds serde serialization derives to edge types used in patches. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/score_q.rs | Adds serde derives to `ScoreQ` for serialization support (but currently drops `Hash`). | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/mod.rs | Exposes the new `graph_patch` module behind the non-wasm cfg gate. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/graph_patch.rs | Introduces patch data structures, CID computation, CBOR serialization, patch application, and Theorem 11 verifier. |

review_comments.body: `ScoreQ` previously derived `Hash`, but the updated derive list drops it. Since `ScoreQ` is a public type, removing `Hash` is a breaking API change for downstream code that may store `ScoreQ` in `HashMap`/`HashSet`.

`compute_cid()` hashes `serde_json::to_vec()` output and silently falls back to an empty byte vector on serialization error (`unwrap_or_default`). This can produce incorrect/unstable CIDs (especially since patches are otherwise serialized as CBOR), and would mask real serialization bugs by hashing empty bytes.

`RouteTranslationMap` uses `HashMap`, but patch CIDs and serialized bytes need deterministic iteration order to be stable across runs/machines. `HashMap` iteration order is randomized, so both CID computation and CBOR encoding can differ even for semantically identical patches.

When applying `added_edges`, the patch-provided `Edge.id` is ignored and a new canonical ID is assigned by `add_edge_with_score`. This can make a patch payload internally inconsistent (CID covers `Edge.id`, but application doesn’t), and can break route-translation IDs if they were derived from the patch’s `Edge.id` values.

Tombstone indices that are out of bounds are silently ignored, which can hide corrupted/invalid patches. Also, `build_reverse_index()` already calls `verify_theorem_7()`, so the subsequent explicit `verify_theorem_7()` is redundant work.

`GraphPatch` encodes edge references as `usize` (`residual_updates: Vec<(usize, ScoreQ)>`, `tombstone_edge_ids: Vec<usize>`). The implementation plan explicitly calls out that artifact/domain values should be fixed-width and “never usize” (to keep formats portable and deterministic across architectures). Consider switching these IDs/indices to `u32` (matching canonical edge IDs) or `u64`.
